title: bj-1: close hook: atm-task-close.py roles dev, fix, sanity, qa; task-close-vars.j2, sanity-fail.xml.j2, rebase-required.xml.j2; max_sanity_rounds
description:
## Goal
One script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes (task-close-hook.md 1). The agent never runs `bd close` or `atm task close ... completed` by hand for those roles. The script checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead. Refused and cancelled dev/fix closes stay `atm task close <id> refused` (task-close-hook.md 11); a sanity CANNOT_RUN goes through the hook as a refused close (17). Governing text: `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` items 1 to 19, `dev.md` 2, 4, 15, 17, 20, 24, `dev-sanity.md` 11, 13, 28, 29, 32, 47, `quality-mgr.md` 20, `team-lead.md` 14, 15, 21, 23, 24, 28. Anchors: ANC-051, 052, 053, 055, 056, 057, 058, 059, 060, 065, 070, 071, 072, 086, 089.

## Deliverables
1. `scripts/atm-task-close.py`: one `--role` argument, mandatory, one of `dev`, `fix`, `sanity`, `qa`; `--vars <file>`; `--skip-checks` described only in `--help` as "skips the PR and stack checks. Do NOT use without permission from the phase lead." and named in no template or prompt (ANC-059). Result is JSON on stdout, `{"ok": {...}}` or `{"err": {"code", "message", "fix"}}`, exit code mirroring it; every `err` names the exact fix (task-close-hook.md 3). Every template render is `sc_render.render`, strict, never piped into `jq`; every subprocess is a fixed argv, never a shell string.
2. Input validation (ANC-058): the vars file is the sc-compose `--vars` payload the role's templates already take; the script validates the unchanged shared vars file with a strict render before any check. One vars file is the `--vars` of every render along dev -> sanity -> QA (ANC-089), so `task-close-vars.j2` `required_variables` are the union of the `required_variables` of these templates, each named once with its owner: `task-close-vars.j2`, `dev-complete.md.j2`, `fix-complete.md.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2`, `sanity-fail.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`, `qa-template.xml.j2`, `qa-complete.md.j2` (all bj-1). The hook renders no bead template; a bead template a later role passes its vars file to joins the union, read from its front matter at test time. A missing or unknown field is an error before any check (task-close-hook.md 2); `commit`, `pr_number` and `branch` must be non-empty except for a fix with `outcome=not_reproducible`, which carries the cited `file:line` instead. The contract keeps distinct `dev_task_id`, `sanity_task_id`, `qa_task_id`, `checked_bead`, `sanity_bead` and `qa_bead`; `task_id` always means the bead whose ATM task the current role template closes, and an assignment template renders its explicit destination id. Every field, including qa-template's `policy_path` and `reviewers_round1`, comes from the lead's dispatch vars file; the hook derives none. Every rendered body id equals the matching command `--task-id` value.
3. Identity (ANC-051): `atm task assign` and the close of the dev's task run with `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead>` and `ATM_TEAM=<team>` set on that one subprocess only, `lead` read from `.atm-bd/phase-<x>.toml` and the team from `.atm.toml`; every other `bd` and `atm` write runs as the caller with `--actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`. The script never changes its own environment.
4. Role `dev` and `fix` (task-close-hook.md 7 to 12): after the vars, checks exactly three things: an open PR exists for `branch` with HEAD as its head; pushed `origin/<branch>` equals clean HEAD; and HEAD descends from the current stack top. The stack top has one owner, `stack_top()` in `atm-task-close.py`: it reads `metadata.layers[-1]` (`branch`, `head`) by key name from `bd show <stack bead> --json`, or returns `pr_target` and its head when `layers` is empty; the ancestor check and the `not_reproducible` assignment both call it. bj-2's `StackMetadata` in `bead_schema.py` is the one schema; bj-1 defines no model class and imports nothing from bj-2, so the two sprints stay parallel. The PR base is not a fourth check, and with a nonempty ledger the check never uses a static branch. `assignment-gates.py` retains only frozen/commit checks that can run before linking; it does not require an already linked PR. No lower layer is checked, and the hook runs no lint or tests (task-close-hook.md 7). On pass: `bd update <bead> --set-metadata commit=<sha> pr_number=<n> pr_url=<url>`; `bd close <bead> --reason "dev complete at <sha>"` (`fixed at <sha>` for a fix); in the same hook invocation, `bd close <dev bead>` is immediately followed by `atm task assign <dev-sanity member> --task-id <sanity bead> --template dev-sanity-template.xml.j2 --vars <same file>` as the lead, with no command, report, or lead action between those two writes (ANC-052); the dev-complete/fix-complete report is sent after the pair by plain `atm send --template`. ANC-052 overrides task-close-hook.md 8's close-report-assign order. The dev's ATM task stays open (ANC-055). The sanity bead is `metadata.sanity_bead` of the checked bead when present, else the open `stage:dev-sanity` bead whose `metadata.dev_bead` is the checked bead; none: `err` naming the lead. Fix outcome `not_reproducible`: the PR and head checks are skipped, `bd close --reason "not reproducible: <file:line>"`, the same report and the same sanity assignment, whose `branch` and `commit` are `stack_top()`'s, so `sanity-split` runs unchanged.
5. GitHub unreachable or rate limited (ANC-059): not a failure; the PR check falls back to the local checks of deliverable 4, the result records `github: unavailable`, and sanity is assigned. Retry a failed GitHub call three times before falling back.
6. Role `sanity` (task-close-hook.md 13 to 17): input the verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`), the sha, the selected undone deliverables with their reasons, the checked bead and its assignee, the group's QA bead, and for PASS the stack result from the link (`stacked`, new top, nullable `stack_number` for a singleton stack). A PASS close without a stack result is refused with `err` code `SANITY.NOT_STACKED` naming the link as the fix (sanity-stack.md 13), except a PASS on a `not_reproducible` fix, which has no layer and is accepted without one. PASS: `bd close <sanity bead> --reason "PASS at <sha>"`; `atm task close <checked bead> completed` as the lead; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`; `atm task assign <qa member> --task-id <qa bead> --template qa-template.xml.j2 --vars <file>` as the lead, with `base` the PR base, `commit`, `round`, `reviewer` and `policy`, and for a fix bead `carry_forward` = the fix bead (ANC-053, task-close-hook.md 14). FAIL: `bd update <sanity bead> --set-metadata sanity_round=<n+1>` first. While the new count is at most `max_sanity_rounds` (repository configuration, default 5 when unset): reopen the checked dev/fix bead to its assignee and reset the claimed sanity bead to `--status open --assignee ""` (dev-sanity 29) before finishing the sanity task; `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2 --vars <file>` on the dev's open task; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` with verdict FAIL; no finding bead, no child bead, no new task, no new layer (ANC-056, ANC-072). When the count exceeds `max_sanity_rounds` (the sixth FAIL by default): the hook reopens nothing (task-close-hook.md 16): the checked bead stays closed and the sanity bead is not reset, so `bd ready` does not list it; the script sends team-lead (ANC-057) `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` with the undone deliverable numbers, closes the sanity task with verdict FAIL and returns `ok` with `"escalated": "SANITY.ROUND_CAP"`, exit 0; the dev's task stays open until team-lead rules. CANNOT_RUN: sanity bead open and unassigned, task `refused` (task-close-hook.md 17, dev-sanity 31); the refused close is the only message and no bead is created (ANC-086). A `rebase-required` outcome is not a close: `verdict` accepts only `PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`, and only FAIL writes `sanity_round` (ANC-071).
7. Role `qa` (ANC-070, quality-mgr 20): input the verdict, the sha, the round; `bd close <qa bead>` first, then `atm task close <qa bead> completed --template qa-complete.md.j2` only if the bead close succeeded; one plain `atm send` status message to the phase lead, PASS and FAIL alike; assigns nothing.
8. `templates/task-close-vars.j2`: header-only strict template, `required_variables` per role through `defaults` and the role switch in deliverable 2; `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`: the sprint and checked bead ids and title, branch, PR and sha checked, round n of `max_sanity_rounds`, and one numbered line per deliverable that was NOT complete with the selected reviewer's reason verbatim, nothing else (ANC-072); `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`: the checked bead, the branch, the recorded top it must rebase onto and the instruction to push and run the hook again (ANC-065). Example vars under `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json`.
9. `max_sanity_rounds` in the repository configuration: `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2` gains the key with default 5; `install.py` renders it from the consumer registry key `max_sanity_rounds` when present, else 5; `repo_config.py` exposes it (ANC-057); `tests/test_install.py` covers the render.
10. Template close steps: `dev-template.xml.j2`, `fix-assignment.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2` and `qa-template.xml.j2` end with "run `atm-task-close.py --role <role> --vars <file>`; on `err` fix the named cause and run it again"; the dev and fix templates say the task stays open until sanity PASS, that a `task_reminder` during the wait is answered by waiting, and that a `sanity-fail` or `rebase-required` message means rebase onto the current top, push and run the hook again (dev 2, 17, 20). In the same change `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2` drops step e3 (the `sanity-run-table.md.j2` render, a template bj-4 deletes) and step f's reference to it. No template names `--skip-checks`. `dev-complete.md.j2` and `fix-complete.md.j2` describe themselves as the body of the hook's `atm send --template` report, not of `atm task close`; `dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`'s FAIL wording says the dev was sent `sanity-fail`, with no filed findings.
11. `scripts/sanity-create-findings` deleted with `test_sanity_create_findings.py` and `test_sanity_selected.py`; `sanity-merge`, `sanity-split` and `sanity-run-history` unchanged (dev-sanity 47). The generated block of `manifest.yaml` is regenerated with `tests/gen_manifest.py` in this layer (it adds the hook, the three templates and the examples and drops the deleted script), never hand-edited. `config/legacy-owned.json` keeps its pre-0.2.3 hashes unchanged.
12. Tests, `scripts/tests/test_task_close.py`, with injected runners (no live bd, atm, gh or GitHub): each role's command sequence and identity per command; the vars validation failing before any git or gh call; `github: unavailable` fallback; the FAIL counter and the cap; the PASS refusal without a stack result; the qa role assigning nothing. The stack-bead fixture `scripts/tests/fixtures/stack-bead.json` is a byte copy of bj-2's `stack-bead.json.j2` design example; nonempty-ledger cases append `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` entries to its `layers` in the test.
13. Replay safety, from existing bead metadata and ATM task events, no second ledger: before each write the hook reads bead state and `atm task events`; a write already recorded with the same key is skipped, one recorded with a different verdict or sha is `REPLAY.CONFLICT`. The key is (role task id, verdict, sha); the FAIL counter's key adds the sanity task's current assignment event id, written as `sanity_round_key` in the same `bd update --set-metadata` as `sanity_round`, so a replay never double-counts and two FAILs on two assignments at one head count twice. A replayed assignment is a same-id update (atm-core #1619), never a second task.

## This Sprint Does Not Close
- The stack bead, its pour and `validate-plan` check (bj-2); the hook only reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers`, by key name (deliverable 4).
- atm-bd dispatch (phase bi, unchanged): it assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task, never a dev or fix bead (ANC-060, ANC-061).
- The link on PASS, the sanity-stack subagent and the dev-sanity prompt (bj-3); this sprint's sanity role only requires the stack result in its vars.
- The console runs tabs and the ledger producers (bj-4).
design:
## Public Contract
```
atm-task-close.py --role dev|fix|sanity|qa --vars <file> [--skip-checks]
stdout: {"ok": {"role": ..., "bead": ..., "commit": ..., "pr_number": ..., "github": "ok"|"unavailable", "assigned": [<task ids>], "closed": [<bead ids>]}}
      | {"err": {"code": "VARS.MISSING"|"VARS.EMPTY"|"VARS.UNKNOWN"|"VARS.INVALID"|"HEAD.DIRTY"|"HEAD.NOT_PUSHED"|"BASE.NOT_ANCESTOR"|"PR.NOT_FOUND"|"SANITY.NOT_STACKED"|"BEAD.NO_SANITY"|"REPLAY.CONFLICT", "message": ..., "fix": ...}}
exit 0 on ok, 1 on err
```
GitHub unavailable is `ok` with `"github": "unavailable"`; the round cap is `ok` with `"escalated": "SANITY.ROUND_CAP"` (exit 0). `PR.NOT_FOUND`: no open PR for `branch` whose head is HEAD; the PR base is not checked.

Identity per command (task-close-hook.md 4):
```python
LEAD_ENV = {**os.environ, "ATM_IDENTITY": lead, "ATM_TEAM": team}   # atm task assign; atm task close <checked bead>
run(["atm", "task", "assign", member, "--task-id", bead, "--template", tpl, "--vars", vars_path], env=LEAD_ENV)
run(["bd", "close", bead, "--reason", reason, "--actor", os.environ["ATM_IDENTITY"]])        # caller
```
`task-close-vars.j2` header:
```
---
name: task-close-vars
format: text
required_variables per role per deliverable 2.
---
```
`main(argv, runner=subprocess.run, clock=time.monotonic)`: the subprocess runner and the clock are an injectable seam that `test_task_close.py` uses and that another test module (bj-3's `test_sanity_stack.py`) can drive the same way.

Ancestor check: `stack_top()` reads `metadata.layers[-1]["branch"]` by key from `bd show <stack bead> --json`, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<branch> HEAD`; `origin/<pr_target>` only when `layers` is empty. No model class. The PR check: `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls?head=<o>:<branch>&state=open` filtered to number, base.ref, head.sha.

## Exact Targets
- new `scripts/atm-task-close.py`, `scripts/tests/test_task_close.py`, `scripts/tests/fixtures/stack-bead.json`, `templates/task-close-vars.j2`, `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`, `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`, `examples/task-close-vars-{dev,fix,sanity,qa}.json`
- edited `templates/dev-template.xml.j2`, `fix-assignment.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2`, `qa-template.xml.j2` (close steps), `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2`, `install.py`, `skills/atm-beads/scripts/repo_config.py`, `scripts/tests/test_templates.py`, `tests/test_install.py`, the generated block of `manifest.yaml` (by `tests/gen_manifest.py`)
- deleted `scripts/sanity-create-findings` and its tests

Also owned: the four completion templates, `assignment-gates.py` and its tests, and tests for the deleted sanity-create-findings script.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `atm-task-close.py --help` lists `--role` as mandatory with the four values; the dev-role check list is exactly: open PR exists, pushed head equals clean HEAD and PR head, and HEAD descends from the current top (`layers[-1]`, falling back to `pr_target` for empty layers); a nonempty-stack fixture with a mismatched lower layer and current top ancestor passes; an unlinked PR passes pre-link frozen/commit gates and is linked after sanity.
- [ ] (ANC-058) a vars file missing a role-required field fails with `VARS.MISSING` before any git or gh call; strict render fixtures cover every role/template using one identical vars path; rendered dev, sanity and QA body task ids equal their command `--task-id` values; a not_reproducible fix with no commit/pr_number/branch renders its report and sanity assignment end to end; a vars file with a field no listed template declares fails `VARS.UNKNOWN` before any check.
- [ ] (ANC-051) in the test's recorded calls, every `atm task assign` and the close of the checked bead's task carry `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead from .atm-bd/phase-x.toml>`; every `bd` write carries `--actor <caller>`.
- [ ] (ANC-052, ANC-055) a dev-role run in a scratch repository with fixture bd and atm: the bead is closed, the sanity task is assigned in the same hook invocation immediately after the bead close using the same vars file, the completion report follows the pair, and no `atm task close <dev task> completed` was issued.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a sanity-role PASS run assigns the qa bead to the qa member as the lead and closes the checked bead's task as the lead.
- [ ] (ANC-056, ANC-072) a sanity-role FAIL run issues exactly one `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2`, reopens the checked bead to its assignee and resets the sanity bead to open/unassigned, creates no bead, and the rendered message lists exactly the undone deliverables with their reasons and the sprint id; the rendered `dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` FAIL body names no finding bead.
- [ ] (ANC-057) six distinct FAIL verdicts with no `max_sanity_rounds` setting reopen the checked bead on the first five and leave `sanity_round` at 6, the checked bead closed and not reopened on the sixth, the sanity bead not reset, the result `ok` with `escalated: SANITY.ROUND_CAP` and exit 0, and exactly one `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` send to team-lead; replaying the sixth FAIL sends no second notice; with `max_sanity_rounds: 2` the third run does the same.
- [ ] (ANC-057) `tests/test_install.py`: an install whose registry has no `max_sanity_rounds` renders `max_sanity_rounds: 5` into `.claude/project/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml`, one with `max_sanity_rounds: 2` renders 2, and `repo_config.load()` returns the rendered value.
- [ ] (ANC-071, ANC-086) in `test_task_close.py`, PASS and CANNOT_RUN runs issue no `sanity_round` write; a `verdict` other than PASS, FAIL or CANNOT_RUN fails `VARS.INVALID` before any write; a CANNOT_RUN run leaves the sanity bead open and unassigned, closes the sanity task `refused`, creates no bead and sends no other message.
- [ ] (replay, deliverable 13) in `test_task_close.py`, a runner failing after each write in turn, then a rerun with the same vars: the dev role ends with one sanity assignment; the sanity FAIL ends with `sanity_round` incremented once and one `sanity-fail` send; the sanity PASS ends with the dev task closed once and one QA assignment; a rerun with a different verdict or sha for a recorded write exits `REPLAY.CONFLICT`.
- [ ] (ANC-089) each `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json` renders strictly through every template that role passes it to; deleting any one variable from it makes the hook exit with `VARS.MISSING` before any check.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a controlled `not_reproducible` fix: the hook assigns sanity with the stack top's branch and head; a sanity PASS with `outcome: not_reproducible` and no stack result closes the sanity bead and the fix's task and assigns QA with `carry_forward` = the fix bead; no `SANITY.NOT_STACKED`, no layer.
- [ ] (ANC-059) with the GitHub runner raising, a dev-role run exits ok with `"github": "unavailable"` after three attempts; a help test verifies the script documents `--skip-checks` with the lead-permission sentence, and `test_templates.py` asserts no rendered template body contains `--skip-checks`.
- [ ] (ANC-070) a qa-role run with verdict FAIL closes the qa bead then the task, sends the lead one status message and issues no `atm task assign`.
- [ ] (dev-sanity 47) `scripts/sanity-create-findings` and its two tests are absent, and `tests/gen_manifest.py --check` passes on this layer with the hook, the three new templates and the examples listed and the deleted script not listed.
- [ ] the four assignment templates render strictly with their example vars and name the hook as the close step; the rendered dev and fix bodies contain no `atm task close ... completed` step; `sanity-fail.xml.j2` and `rebase-required.xml.j2` render strictly with their example vars, the latter naming the checked bead, the branch and the recorded top (ANC-065).

## Validation
- `just lint` and `just test` in the atm-bd-orchestration worktree.
- `python3 -m pytest plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/tests/test_task_close.py -q`
